channel.title: Stanislav Peev - SEO & AI Search (GEO) Research
channel.description: Original research and data reports on AI search visibility, GEO (generative engine optimization) and SEO - by Stanislav Peev, independent SEO consultant and AI search specialist.

item.title: How to hire an SEO expert: a step-by-step process for 2026
item.description: A hiring guide for SEO help built on Google's own advice ("Do you need an SEO?", updated June 5, 2026): consultant, freelancer, agency or employee by problem; where to find candidates (on October 28, 2026, 5 of the top 10 US Google results for "hire seo consultant" were marketplaces and talent networks; "seo specialist" results were job and salary pages); a one-page brief; eight questions with good and bad answers; a paid audit or trial with read-only Search Console access; contract and ownership terms; Google's red flags; how to hire for AI search (GEO); and what the first 90 days should show.

item.title: Can you get cited in AI answers without ranking in Google? Usually, yes
item.description: Original data: 407 Google mobile queries in Bulgarian, Slovak, English and Romanian search (October 26, 2026, results to position 100, AI Overviews loaded), ChatGPT with web search on 200 of them. Of 2,961 web pages cited in AI Overviews, 28% ranked in the organic top 10 for the same query (95% CI 25-32%), 7% in positions 11-100 and 65% outside the top 100 (Ahrefs, March 2026: 37% / 26% / 37%). Citation odds by organic position: #1 34%, #3 27%, #10 14%, #11 7%, #20 1%. Of non-ranking citations, 46% came from a domain ranking in the top 100 with another page; 15% social or video. ChatGPT: 91% of 932 cited pages outside Google's top 100, 4% in the top 10, 9% also cited in the AI Overview; searches differed from the query in 98.5% of cases, added "2026" in 44%. One week later the median AI Overview kept half of its cited pages, 20% kept none. CC BY 4.0 data.

item.title: Why is your site-wide CTR so low? It is rarely page 2
item.description: Original Search Console data from 15 sites (web search, September 26 to October 23, 2026; 2,853,158 impressions, 101,412 clicks). Median site-wide CTR 4.1% (range 0.36% to 24.5%) vs 1.2% for non-branded queries; branded queries 3.5% of impressions and 24% of clicks at a 25% CTR (median site). Non-branded, median site: positions 1-3 hold 19% of impressions and 37% of clicks (6.6% CTR); positions 4-10 hold 58% of impressions and 52% of clicks (1.4% CTR); positions 11+ 20% and 6% (0.38%). Keeping only top-10 queries lifts non-branded CTR by a median 17% (1.2% to 1.5%). Visible query rows cover a median 57% of impressions and 48% of clicks (anonymized queries). Year over year (14 sites): median 3.5% to 3.8%, 9 of 14 down. Benchmarks: Ahrefs 1-2% typical (422,421 sites), Databox 0.91% median. Diagnosis method, calculator and CC BY 4.0 data.

item.title: How much do AI Overviews cut your CTR? Same query, one year apart
item.description: Original Search Console data from 15 sites, mostly in Bulgarian search. On the same query at a stable position, mobile CTR fell 28% (95% interval -36% to -18%) from September-October 2025 to September-October 2026 where Google now shows an AI Overview, and -10% (-24% to +6%) where it does not; 280 query pairs, 13 sites. Impressions +54% and clicks -12% on the AI Overview queries; top 3 -35%; cited in the overview -32% vs not cited -24%. Snapshot of 1,317 non-branded page-one queries: AI Overview on 71% (Bulgarian 74%, Slovak 55%, English 80%), 97% of question queries, 19% of queries with a local pack. A one-period with-vs-without split shows the reverse (4.7x), which is why the comparison must be same query over time. Method, calculator and CC BY 4.0 data.

item.title: Do your own "reviews" site, a "best X" list that ranks you first, or a paid award get you into AI answers?
item.description: A buyer's guide written by someone who does not sell reviews, rankings or awards. Google's AI Overviews cited self-promotional "best" lists 323 times in a 100-query test and did not recommend the author in 224 of them (69%). How often AI answers cite pages a brand controls, why that rarely becomes a recommendation, what Google does with self-promotion, US FTC 16 CFR 465.6 and EU and UK review law (up to $53,088 per violation in the US), research on manipulating AI search, whether paid awards help, an 8-question risk checklist, and seven popular claims that do not hold as stated. Updated October 19, 2026 with July to October 2026 data on 11,025 queries. 37 sources, vendors flagged.

item.title: Is it worth paying a Reddit agency to get into ChatGPT and AI Overviews?
item.description: A buyer's guide written by someone who does not sell Reddit posting. One tracker (Promptwatch) saw Reddit's share of ChatGPT Search citations fall from 3.83% to 0.52% in August 2026, while Google AI Overviews fell 11.3% and AI Mode 30.5%. Covers which engine a retainer can move, the volatility record since May 2025, published agency prices ($2,500 to $12,500 a month), account ownership under Reddit's user agreement, FTC disclosure (16 CFR 255 and Part 465), how to verify citation claims on your own prompts, a 10-question pre-hire checklist with three deal-breakers, alternatives, and six popular claims that do not hold as stated. 33 sources, vendors flagged.

item.title: Do competitor comparison pages sway AI answers? A 144-answer test, and what to do when AI repeats a competitor's claim
item.description: Original experiment: 144 answers from Perplexity, GPT-4o and Gemini to "X vs Y: which is better?" for 12 software vendor pairs. 76% cited a page written by one of the two vendors, yet when a vendor's own page was cited it won 68 times and lost 66, and 94 of 96 clear verdicts went to the same winner per pair. What a competitor's page really moves is the facts, with a step-by-step fix for false claims (fact page, third-party repetition, NAD, Lanham Act, EU Directive 2006/114/EC) and for answers dominated by one negative review. Raw data published. Data published under CC BY 4.0.

item.title: What percentage of leads really come from ChatGPT? Tracked vs self-reported data
item.description: Seventeen published figures sorted into three layers and checked against their original source. Tracked by analytics: 0.073% of about 20 million inbound calls (CallRail), under 2% of 25 million B2B sessions (Octane11). Asked or disclosed by the company: 7.29% of Outfunnel leads, 8% to 25% of new signups at Webflow, Vercel and Tally. Buyer surveys: 45% to 94%. Why the layers differ - 55.9% of visits after a ChatGPT recommendation arrive as branded search (Similarweb) - plus a gap calculator and four popular figures that did not trace to their credited source. Data published under CC BY 4.0.

item.title: AI citations by question shape: which pages ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity cite for "best X", "X alternatives" and "X vs Y"
item.description: Original pilot: 176 citations from three web-connected AI engines, every cited page labeled by shape and owner. "best X" questions cited listicles 84% of the time and comparison pages 2%; "X alternatives" questions cited comparison-shaped pages 86%, with 24% of citations going to comparison pages on competing vendors' own domains and a single citation to G2; "X vs Y" questions 98%. Explains why the published "under 3%" share for comparison pages is an average across question types. Method, limitations and raw data published under CC BY 4.0.

item.title: AI referral traffic vs organic search: how it converts for a small business
item.description: Aggregated, source-verified 2026 data on how AI-referral traffic converts against organic search: about 50% higher on Shopify product pages, 4.4x per-visitor value (Semrush), and 14.2% vs 2.8% lead conversion in B2B (Opollo) - with the catch that volume is still tiny and AI converted 43% worse than other channels as recently as July 2024. What it means for a small business, limitations named.

item.title: Google review concentration: who really owns the reviews in a local market
item.description: Original dataset: 7,072 Google Business Profile listings across 6 home service trades in 12 US cities. The most-reviewed company held a top-3 Maps position in just 5.6% of 72 markets; the top 5 listings hold a median 58.3% of visible review volume; trade predicts difficulty far better than city size. Full method, limitations and raw data published.

item.title: How reliable is AI visibility tracking? A 60-query experiment
item.description: An original experiment: the same four buyer questions run 60 times across ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity. Which engine you track moved a brand's measured AI visibility 2.3x more than the model's own run-to-run randomness, and two engines recommended a tool the third never named once. Full method, limitations and raw dataset published.

item.title: SEO Profy: what a real SEO professional does and how to hire one
item.description: A working SEO professional's guide for US businesses: what the job includes in 2026 (including AI search), when DIY is enough, engagement models, what business owners really say about hiring SEO help, and the red flags to walk away from.

item.title: How often AI gets business information wrong: 2026 statistics
item.description: 93% of businesses have at least one fact wrong or missing in AI answers. Source-verified statistics on how often ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity misstate business hours, phone numbers and services - with a 10-prompt self-audit protocol to test your own business.
